nodes.label: CI Build Job
nodes.rationale: Runs test:unit rather than test because the preceding build already produced the dist/ and public/ artifacts the tests import, so rebuilding is skipped; publint validates the published package shape.

nodes.label: Publish Workflow Job
nodes.rationale: Gated on repository_owner == 'playcanvas'; version tags trigger a provenance-enabled npm publish where beta tags go to the beta dist-tag and others to latest; builds with NODE_ENV=production before publint and publish.

nodes.label: Camera Commands (frameScene / resetCamera / toggleWalk)
nodes.rationale: Throw before state.loaded or after destruction, matching seek; frameScene now reports invalid calls instead of silently doing nothing. toggleWalk reproduces the built-in walk button, returning to the previous mode including one the host entered by writing state directly.

nodes.label: captureFrame
nodes.rationale: Renders offscreen, supersampled, waits for the first frame, and resolves { width, height, data } with base64 data.

nodes.label: createViewer
nodes.rationale: The /viewer subpath entry with playcanvas as a peer dependency so the host's engine copy is the one used. Resolves once the graphics device exists and loading has started, not once the scene is visible; the viewer builds its own subtree so the container needs a size or nothing renders.
nodes.source_location: Creating a viewer in your own page

nodes.label: defaultSettings
nodes.rationale: Returns a complete settings object every tool agrees on; pass 'object' to frame a subject from outside rather than a captured space from within.

nodes.label: destroy
nodes.rationale: Browsers cap live WebGL contexts at around 16, so a component that mounts and unmounts without tearing down will stop rendering; destroy is idempotent, releases the engine application, graphics context, every listener, the subtree, and rejects outstanding API waits.

nodes.label: importSettings
nodes.rationale: Migrates older settings versions forward without mutating its argument.

nodes.label: POST_EFFECT_RANGES
nodes.rationale: Bounds (with CAMERA_FOV_RANGE, ANIM_TRACK_LIMITS, ANNOTATION_LIMITS) are exported as frozen data so an editor UI can drive sliders from the same numbers the validator uses.

nodes.label: renderViewerHtml
nodes.rationale: The only supported way to generate a page around the viewer; the raw html string export is deprecated because its formatting changes between releases and pattern-matching it is unsupported. inlineCss/inlineJs yield a single self-contained file with the splat as a data: URI named via contentFilename, since the splat format is chosen by the name's extension and a data: URI has no filename.

nodes.label: seek
nodes.rationale: Synchronous and preserves pause state, so pause first to stop at the requested time; wraps repeat tracks and clamps once and ping-pong tracks to their duration. The standalone window.scrubTo hook retains pause-and-wait-for-frame behavior instead.

nodes.label: selectAnnotation
nodes.rationale: The same command the built-in hotspots and previous/next buttons use; null clears selection without starting another camera movement; runtime annotation editing is unsupported and the data is read-only in settings order.

nodes.label: setMoveInput
nodes.rationale: An explicit command that works independently of gamingControls, inputMode and inputEnabled; values clamp to [-1,1] and stay active until replaced, and the viewer clears held input on camera/XR mode changes, window blur, visibility changes and destruction. The built-in touch joystick uses the same command.

nodes.label: validateSettings
nodes.rationale: Throws on invalid input naming the offending field; the { limits: true } authoring-bounds check is stricter than what the viewer will render (existing files may fail) and producers writing new settings should enable it.

nodes.label: Fullscreen & XR Commands (requestFullscreen / startXR / endXR)
nodes.rationale: startXR never reloads the page - the built-in UI owns the WebGL reload prompt; the legacy iframe fullscreen parent-message bridge resolves when sent because it has no acknowledgement; standalone headsets render with fixed foveation, 72 Hz target and a 1 million splat budget (0.8x resolution in performance mode).

nodes.label: attachProfiler
nodes.rationale: The engine's timestamp profiler reports asynchronously a few frames late and pass names live in pastFrameAllocations consumed by report(), so the report is wrapped to copy names and accumulate per-pass timings when they arrive.

nodes.label: Renderer Bench Harness (bench.html)
nodes.rationale: Loads the scene once per mode (the engine's sorted renderer, then the opt-in stochastic renderer), sets each camera pose, and measures every variant with the engine's GPU timestamp profiler while a MessageChannel pump drives frames as fast as the GPU takes them, so the queue stays saturated regardless of vsync or tab visibility. Stochastic frames are diffed against the sorted frame at the same pose and against a second stochastic frame with another seed for the noise floor; three round-robin rounds per pose with median-of-medians and min-of-mins.

nodes.label: capture
nodes.rationale: Deliberately not viewer.captureFrame(): that renders a query frame into its own target with a horizontal fov the temporal history would have to be resampled into, and it would enter the history as an extra sample. Instead one more frame is rendered and the canvas read back in the same task, because WebGPU keeps no drawing buffer past it.

nodes.label: captureStore (IndexedDB)
nodes.rationale: A run's worth of 1080p frames is far beyond localStorage, so save=/against= captures live in IndexedDB; a variant accumulates the same seeds each run, so diffing against an earlier build's tag shows an unchanged renderer differing by nothing.

nodes.label: depthRoughness
nodes.rationale: Mean absolute step of the 24-bit log depth view between neighbouring covered pixels - a depth surface's roughness, where plates show as steps.

nodes.label: flythrough / flyPath
nodes.rationale: A first pass streams the path's detail in (kept as the cold pass), then round-robin timed passes so drift touches each variant alike; the per-frame median over passes is the headline so a one-frame hitch in one pass does not move it; pathHold times the same views moving and still; keyframes follow a Catmull-Rom spline with unwrapped yaw.

nodes.label: imageDiff
nodes.rationale: The 8/255 changed-pixel threshold is the editor's convention; a separate 48-level far threshold catches ghosts and gross errors that the rms spreads over the whole image; the signed per-channel mean exposes intensity or tint bias.

nodes.label: measure
nodes.rationale: Console markers around the measured frames support a host sampling GPU hardware counters alongside; timestamps come in 65.5 us ticks, so the mean over many frames resolves differences smaller than one tick that the median and minimum cannot.

nodes.label: orbitStep
nodes.rationale: A moving camera exercises the work-buffer colour refresh, LOD changes, the occlusion cull's reprojection and the temporal history; strafe motion moves sideways at the orbit's speed at the focus so the parallax uncovers what the foreground hid.

nodes.label: overdrawPath
nodes.rationale: Reads the projected cache back and sums its quads in pixels over the screen's, clipped where alpha falls below the clip as both renderers draw them; with the cull off the cache holds every splat the sorted renderer draws.

nodes.label: pump / pumpFrame
nodes.rationale: One frame sequenced as AppBase.tick does it, without waiting for the display; FRAMES_IN_FLIGHT=2 bounds queued frames because without a bound a phone's CPU runs hundreds of frames ahead and the profiler's reports for one variant arrive during the next; MessageChannel yields are used because timers in a hidden tab fire once a second at best.

nodes.label: toSnapshot
nodes.rationale: Accepts the debug panel's window.getCameraState snapshot shape, or converts {position, target, fov} the way Camera.look does (see src/core/math.ts vecToAngles).

nodes.label: Custom UI Example (custom-ui.html)
nodes.rationale: Demonstrates ui:false using only the public viewer handle and documented state events - no engine access, private events or queries into the viewer's markup; it is a development example, not a React package or a published UI component; its controls live outside the fullscreen viewer root, so Escape or the browser's exit affordance is needed to leave fullscreen.

nodes.label: metaTeardown
nodes.rationale: meta.json content is read with an await before the asset is registered, so a destroy can land inside it and the continuation must not touch the app it just lost; driven with a contents promise the page controls so the timing is exact rather than a race with the network.

nodes.label: Mount/Unmount Teardown Harness (mount-loop.html)
nodes.rationale: Browsers cap live WebGL contexts at around 16, so twenty iterations that all reach a first frame is itself the leak test; each iteration reports whether the previous context was released and whether the subtree was removed. Run by hand before any change to teardown-sensitive code merges - it is the only teardown check, as there is no automated one.

nodes.label: sse-bootstrap Injection Seam
nodes.rationale: Single injection seam: renderViewerHtml replaces the contents of this block to supply asset urls and inline settings, so generators go through that function rather than pattern-matching the document. URL params take precedence over the bootstrap's asset URLs so an embed stays overridable per instance - except an inline settings object, which wins over ?settings= so a published experience cannot be repointed at someone else's settings file.

nodes.label: Standalone Viewer Document (index.html)
nodes.rationale: Page-filling styles live here rather than in index.css because a host page linking the stylesheet must not have its own body restyled; the poster image and the content fetch start here, before the module bundle has arrived; the engine's octree parser fetches lod-meta.json itself and ignores a prefetched response, so it is not prefetched (isPrefetchable in src/index.ts applies the same rule); the standalone document is the one place the window.* hooks belong (exposeGlobals: true).

nodes.label: Viewer Markup Template (ui.html)
nodes.rationale: Nothing here carries an id because a document can hold the template many times (createViewer parses it into a div.sse-viewer per instance); every class carries the sse- prefix so host page styles cannot collide, and ui.ts looks elements up by 'sse-' + name under the instance root; layering is by order back to front so nothing needs a z-index.

nodes.label: ExperienceSettings Schema
nodes.rationale: settings.json v2 schema defined in TypeScript and exported from the /settings subpath; legacy v1 settings produced by older SuperSplat releases are automatically migrated forward on load.

nodes.label: Saved Preferences
nodes.rationale: performanceMode, gamingControls and showAnnotations load from and write to existing origin-wide localStorage keys with or without the built-in UI; creation does not write defaults; the legacy retinaDisplay migration is preserved; storage denial or quota errors leave the viewer usable; already-mounted viewers keep their own state rather than syncing through storage; destruction removes persistence subscriptions.

nodes.label: Viewer Handle
nodes.rationale: Host and built-in playback controls use the same API: observable state with writable keys that apply at once plus <key>:changed events. Nothing is published to window unless exposeGlobals is set; keyboard/gamepad listeners cannot be routed by hit-testing, so hosts gate them with state.inputEnabled.

nodes.label: Stochastic Renderer
nodes.rationale: Experimental unsorted, depth-tested splat renderer, WebGPU only (XR included): 'stochastic' for per-pixel quality, 'stochastic=mobile' for phones and headsets; splatSource (direct vs workbuffer) and variant are developer knobs feeding it.

nodes.label: URL Parameters
nodes.rationale: URL parameters override embedder-supplied asset URLs so an embed stays overridable per instance; the programmatic form (ui:false, reticle:true, etc.) mirrors the flags.

nodes.label: SuperSplat Viewer
nodes.rationale: Official viewer for SuperSplat; compiles to a simple, self-contained static website. Uses WebGPU by default with automatic fallback, but WebGL must be forced for WebXR/AR/VR.
